claims.text: Replacing traditional EAM reference potentials with MLIPs trained directly on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in the liquid state near and at their melting temperatures.
The reference MLIP should be trained on a diverse set of ab initio liquid configurations.
A neural-network potential or Gaussian approximation potential can serve as the reference system in thermodynamic integration.
High-temperature alloy liquids exhibit a high diversity of atomic configurations.
The proposed composition range is multicomponent systems containing at least four elements that exhibit high-entropy behavior.
Local-environment and many-body descriptors allow an MLIP to represent a broad spectrum of atomic configurations.
The proposed descriptor framework can represent atomic configurations beyond the capabilities of standard EAM potentials.
Training on ab initio liquid configurations enables the MLIP to capture many-body interactions.
Training on ab initio liquid configurations enables the MLIP to capture structural fluctuations near melting.
Many-body interactions and structural fluctuations dominate the liquid near its melting point.
Representing these interactions and fluctuations will improve phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
The MLIP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reduced path mismatch will improve convergence of free-energy calculations.
The intervention will improve agreement between ab initio and reference-based free-energy estimates.
Traditional TOR-TILD EAM references have limited ability to represent the configuration space of ab initio liquids at elevated temperatures.
The MLIP approach may be less effective for compositions or temperatures outside its training range.
Direct supporting evidence for this intervention in multicomponent high-entropy alloys under the specified conditions is unavailable.
Evidence from elemental or binary systems may not transfer fully to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.

The hypothesis is falsified if the MLIP reference fails to reduce path mismatch by at least 50% relative to the EAM reference, or fails to produce a statistically significant improvement in overlap and free-energy convergence.
